html:
The Tinigua were a small people of the Yarí and Caguán river basins in southern Colombia, in today's Caquetá and Meta, where the Llanos meet the Amazon forest. In their language Tinigua refers to the ancestors.

Their language forms a tiny family with the extinct Pamigua. Wars with neighbours and settlers in the 1900s nearly wiped them out, and by the early 2000s only one or two speakers were left, near the Sierra de la Macarena. Their neighbours included the Guahibo of the plains to the north and the Karijona to the south.
